note: Inputs only: endpoint table (12 h), not a time series. Not converted to data/real.

files.extracted.csv: tidy long: one row per cathode x quantity

csv_columns.table_row: row order in the printed table
csv_columns.cathode: cathode material as printed (Greek 'Γραφίτης' = graphite; 'Ru σε γραφίτη' = Ru on graphite)
csv_columns.E_mV_vs_AgAgCl: applied potential, mV vs Ag/AgCl (saturated KCl)
csv_columns.quantity: removal (%RE of NO3-) or selectivity (%S of a product)
csv_columns.species: NO3 for removal; NO2, NH3 or gaseous_products for selectivity
csv_columns.selectivity_basis: basis of %S as defined on printed p. 84
csv_columns.flag: 'uncertain' where the printed cell is internally inconsistent

provenance.citation: Polatides C., Electrochemical removal of nitrate from aqueous solutions and environmental samples using constant and pulsed potential, PhD thesis (in Greek), Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Dept. of Chemical Engineering (2007); supervisor G. Kyriacou
provenance.caption_translated: Table 5.1. Degree of nitrate removal (%RE) and selectivity (%S) of the products on various cathode electrodes. Initial solution 0.1 M K2SO4 and 0.05 M KNO3. Electrolysis duration 12 h. Columns: cathode material | E/mV vs. Ag/AgCl | %RE NO3- | %S NO2- | %S NH3 | %S gaseous products.
provenance.source_file: page text layer from the archive's online reader (scratch only, not committed)
provenance.licence: National Archive of PhD Theses terms: research use with no direct or indirect financial benefit; author must be cited; items protected by copyright

conditions.potential_choice: potential chosen so that the initial current was about 40 mA in every case (printed p. 83)
conditions.cell: not stated in section 5.1; the thesis cell (ch. 4) is a Teflon cell, divided by Nafion 117 (20 mL catholyte, 20 mL anolyte) unless stated otherwise
conditions.electrode_notes: Ru, Os and Pd deposited on graphite (carbon felt); Cu60Zn40 is a 100 mesh brass gauze, Sn85Cu15 a solder alloy (ch. 4)

definitions_translated.printed_p84: %RE nitrate = mols NO3- reduced / mols NO3- in the initial solution x 100; %S product = mols product formed / mols NO3- reduced x 100. 'In the case of nitrogen the mols N2 produced were multiplied by two, because 2 mols of nitrate are required to produce 1 mol N2.'
definitions_translated.gas_basis_printed_p84_85: Gaseous products were NO, NO2 (traces), N2O (about 500 ppm in the gas stream, usually a selectivity of 1-2 %) and N2. For graphite the text calls the 30.02 % gaseous selectivity the value 'as it resulted from the mass balance', i.e. 100 - %S NO2 - %S NH3.
definitions_translated.not_detected: hydrazine and hydroxylamine were not detected in any final solution (printed p. 83)

checks.pb_row_note: Pb selectivities sum to 99.67 % (100 - NO2 - NH3 = 31.51 against the printed gas 31.18). The 'as it resulted from the mass balance' remark on printed p. 85 is about graphite (30.02 %) only; the same page repeats Pb gas 31.18 % and RE 93.28 %, and Table 5.21 gives Pb NH3 68.5 (divided cell). Which Pb value is off, or whether the Pb gas value was not taken by difference, is not settled by the text. Note narrowed 2026-10-20 after the independent re-check (data/digitized_inputs/thesis_tables_verification.json); no value changed.
checks.comparison_with_table_5p21_divided_cell: Same electrodes, potentials, electrolyte and 12 h in Table 5.21 (divided cell): RE and NO2 agree (Cu60Zn40 99.1/9.6, Al 88.6/2.3, Pb 93.3/0.1 vs 99.10/9.62, 88.66/2.26, 93.28/0.00); NH3 agrees for Al (53.3) and Pb (68.5) but not Cu60Zn40 (75.2 vs 72.24); gaseous selectivity differs (Cu60Zn40 3.0 vs 18.14, Al 43.0 vs 44.45, Pb 17.2 vs 31.18). Table 5.1 gases close the balance to 100 %, Table 5.21 divided-cell gases do not.

transcription_method: thesis text layer: per-page text layer of the National Archive of PhD Theses online reader (EKT freader), read and typed in by an agent on 2026-10-20; table layout reconstructed by hand from the flattened text; every row's printed number sequence was checked by script to occur verbatim on the cited page (literature/extraction_scripts/thesis_tables/build_tables.py). Page images of these pages were not viewed. Not yet re-checked by a person.
